propositions: The outbound comment dedup key is computed as a prediction of wire bytes in the differ, but the send path independently recomputes those bytes through different code paths, causing convergence bugs when the two compositions drift.
Both mutation-enactment consumers (create and update paths) must receive the fitted wire body from a single canonical source to ensure the dedup key matches what is actually transmitted.
The adapter's fit operation must be idempotent so that re-fitting an already-fitted body returns it byte-identical, preventing the key from becoming stale after send-time encoding.
The dedup key must be derived from the exact bytes handed to the transport, not predicted in advance; it should equal the marker-stripped decode of the wire body as sent.
Mutation entries written before the cutover must still send their body when wire_body is absent, maintaining backward compatibility with in-flight queues.
